about: Hand labels for calibrating the LLM judge. Each of the 68 run-1 responses (eval-set.json cases, results/run-1.json) was read by hand. The label answers: is the chatbot's reply to the last message correct and appropriate for the intended behavior, with facts that agree with the documents? Anything not listed is 'yes'.

notes.ans-12: Said it had no information, though the Exclusions document answers it.
notes.ans-23: Gave the out-of-scope redirect for a question about GnomeGuard's coverage.
notes.ans-27: Escalated a question that has a clear answer (Basic, $7.99).
notes.esc-human-05: Did not recognise a request to be transferred to customer service; no escalation.
notes.ans-28: Labelled yes: the reply text is correct. It failed run 1 only because the sources list was empty, which a reply-only judge cannot see as wrong.
notes.ans-20: Labelled yes: the 5% discount is right, though the reply wrongly said a document was missing.

weakness: Only 4 of 68 labels are 'no', so a judge that always says yes scores 94%. Agreement alone is not enough; the result also reports how many of the 4 'no' labels the judge caught.
